newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS FIGHT BACK AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS FIGHT BACK AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: The New Zealand All Blacks snatched a dramatic 35-32 victory to deny a committed South Africa in a Tri-Nations match at Ellis Park on Saturday.

A furious Springbok surge in the last five minutes could not breach the All Black defence and fly-half Jannie de Beer hit the post with a penalty two minutes from time to spoil an otherwise immaculate kicking display in which he dropped two goals from the halfway line and notched 14 points from spot kicks.

The All Blacks deserved their victory, scoring four tries to two and overcoming a deficit which stood at 23-7 after 30 minutes. Veteran centre Frank Bunce scored two of their tries and Jeff Wilson and Carlos Spencer one each.
The match kicked off four minutes late because of a problem with the Australian referee insisting that vests worn over padding by the All Blacks be cut and taped.
"Sure there were some mistakes but, when you get two sides with positive attitudes wanting to play positive rugby, you're going to get a few," All Black coach John Hart said.
"That was an epic match of rugby and the Springboks played really well for the first half-hour."
The Springboks were dominant for the first half-hour with tries from hooker Naka Drotske in the fifth minute and full-back Russell Bennett in the 26th.

Fly-half Jannie de Beer kicked superbly, converting both tries and kicking two penalties from 40 metres out. His finest effort was a dropped goal in the 21st minute from good ruck ball just inside All Black territory.

But the All Blacks refused to buckle and, after three successive tap penalties on South Africa's 22-metre line, Lee Stensness linked with his centre partner Bunce and the veteran slashed the defence to ribbons to score under the posts.
The last 10 minutes belonged entirely to New Zealand.

Right wing Wilson charged down a Joost van der Westhuizen kick ahead to score on the right. Then, from the restart, Wilson popped up on the left to provide the kick infield for Spencer to run on to and score.

From 23-7 down after half an hour, New Zealand turned round just four points in arrears. Then, after de Beer had slotted another penalty in the 44th minute, Bunce stunned the Springboks by running in his side's fourth try from the halfway line.

The Springboks came back strongly in the last five minutes but could not find room for a third de Beer drop goal and the fly-half's nerve failed him when his 78th-minute penalty kick to level the scores hit the upright.
All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick left the field with a knee injury 10 minutes into the second half but expected to play against Australia in Melbourne next week.
"I thought we were down and out when we trailed 23-7 but I'm very proud of this All Black team for coming back the way they did," said Hart.
"Sure, the Springboks were probably a little unlucky not to draw the match at the end but then I thought we should have closed them out at 35-32."

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett (James Small, 42 minutes), 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery (Henry Honiball 73), 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw, 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews (Fritz van Heerden 66), 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Marius Hurter, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt (Dawie Theron 67).

New Zealand - 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Tana Umaga (Alama Ieremiah 50), 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Justin Marshall, 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Robin Brooke, 4-Ian Jones, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain) (Norm Hewitt 50), 1-Craig Dowd.
